drapeaux.note: The French teaser says the mammoths survived “five millennia longer” than the date of 10,000 years ago, but the body text gives a disappearance about four thousand years ago (six millennia later, as Martin and Stuart put it); five millennia is the survival time on the island after its isolation around 9,000 years before present. Translated as written.

titre: The Last Mammoths Lived on Wrangel Island Until the Time of the Pharaohs
accroche: The mammoth was thought to have gone extinct ten thousand years ago. On an Arctic island, mammoths described as dwarfs survived five millennia longer.
contenu_vulgarise:
The picture has become classic: at the end of the last ice age, about ten thousand years ago, the woolly mammoth disappears. It was thought to have made its last stand on the Arctic coast of Siberia, around 10,000 years before present. That date does not hold for the whole population.

## An Island in the Arctic Ocean

Wrangel Island lies in the Arctic Ocean, off the northeast coast of Siberia. Between 1989 and 1991, researchers collect mammoth tusks, teeth and bones there, and date them by radiocarbon. The article by S. L. Vartanyan and his colleagues, published in 1995 in the journal Radiocarbon, concludes that these remains reveal a unique refuge for the mammoth during the Holocene. The article's title gives the limit: mammoths were still living on the island until 2000 BCE. Two years earlier, in 1993, Vartanyan, Garutt and Sher had already published in Nature the case of Holocene dwarf mammoths on this island.

## The Last Ones, and How Long They Lasted

A tooth from the island gave the most recent radiocarbon age known: 3,685 ± 60 years before present (Vartanyan and colleagues, 2008, reported by Nyström and colleagues, 2010). This is a raw radiocarbon age, which is not read as a calendar date, but the order of magnitude is clear. According to this 2010 study, the island had become isolated around 9,000 years before present and the population survived there for more than five thousand years before dying out. Paul Martin and Anthony Stuart wrote as early as 1995 that these remains stretched the chronology of mammoth extinction by six millennia, to the time of the pharaohs.

The authors of 1993 describe these mammoths as dwarfs and attribute this dwarfism to insularity, combined with the deteriorating conditions of the Holocene.

## What We Still Don't Know

The cause of their disappearance remains open, and it is the most instructive part. The 2010 study rules out a simple answer: there is no direct evidence of a human arrival on the island before the extinction. The first dated human presence is 3,360 ± 155 years before present, with no trace of mammoth hunting. The hypotheses that remain are a new disease, a brief climate change that the records did not capture, or the genetic effects of a tiny population, whose carrying capacity is estimated at between 149 and 819 individuals. The authors conclude that the precise mechanism remains unresolved.

The “extinction” of the mammoth did not have a single date. Depending on where one looks, it disappears ten thousand years ago or about four thousand years ago. What remains to be understood is what the last of them encountered.

repere.texte: A mammoth tooth from Wrangel Island gave the most recent radiocarbon age known: 3,685 ± 60 years before present. On the mainland, mammoths were thought to have disappeared around 10,000 years before present.

carte.idee: The mammoth was thought to have gone extinct around 10,000 years before present. A tooth from Wrangel Island dates to 3,685 ± 60 years: a population survived there for more than five millennia, for a cause of extinction still unknown.

quiz.question: What does the dating of the teeth and tusks from Wrangel Island show?
choix: That the island's mammoths had just been brought there by the first humans
That mammoths lived there for millennia after their supposed disappearance from the mainland
That the island's first inhabitants hunted the mammoths to extinction
That the mammoth disappeared everywhere at the same moment, about ten thousand years ago
quiz.explication: The island's remains are more recent than the date accepted for the mainland. Nothing shows that they were brought there: they were isolated on the island around 9,000 years before present. No evidence links their disappearance to hunting, and the date is precisely not the same everywhere.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What do researchers attribute the dwarfism of the Wrangel Island mammoths to?
choix: Insularity, combined with the deteriorating conditions of the Holocene
A genetic mutation that appeared after their isolation on the island
Hunting, which would have selected the smallest individuals
A disease that would have slowed their growth
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The authors of 1993 attribute the dwarfism of the Wrangel mammoths to insularity and to the deteriorating conditions of the Holocene, not to an isolated genetic cause or to hunting.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What do the archaeological traces show about possible human hunting on the island before the extinction?
choix: Spearheads found near the mammoth bones
Butchery marks on several skeletons dated to before 3,685 years before present
No evidence of a human arrival before the extinction, and no trace of hunting at the first dated presence
Human camps dated to more than 9,000 years before present
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The 2010 study rules out an early human arrival: the first dated presence, 3,360 plus or minus 155 years before present, bears no trace of mammoth hunting.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What is the estimate of the island's carrying capacity for the mammoth population?
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The 2010 study estimates the island's carrying capacity at between 149 and 819 individuals, a population small enough for genetic effects to be a hypothesis for the extinction.
